chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

A man wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) complaining to him of insinuations (lammam) that flashed across his mind. So he (peace be upon him) answered in one of his speeches: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, if He wills, will establish you firmly, so He will not make for Iblees a way upon you.'

A group of people had complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) of insinuations that presented to them; it was more beloved to them if the wind were to sweep them away or a limb were cut off, than that they should speak about it. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do you find that?' They said, 'Yes.' So he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul! That is explicit faith (Iman). So whenever you find it, say: We have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah.'
'We have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and there is no might and no strength except with Allah.'

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no might and no strength except with Allah (a key dhikr)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of satanic insinuations (lammam) in Shia theology and how does one respond to them?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between mere cognitive occurrence of satanic whispers and the spiritual burden of acting upon them, a key concept in Shia theology regarding the purity of faith. It highlights the Prophetic precedent where companions preferred silence over speech to avoid sin, reinforcing the practice of reciting 'Aminallahu wa rasuluhu' as a shield. The Imam’s promise of divine stabilization underscores the reliance on God’s grace to prevent Iblees from gaining a foothold in the believer's heart.

en.hubeali: A number of companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘A man wrote to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> complaining to him<sup>asws</sup> of what tends to come upon his mind. So he<sup>asws</sup> answered in one of his<sup>asws</sup> speeches that: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, if He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to, would Affirm you, so He<sup>azwj</sup> would not Make for Iblees<sup>la</sup> to have a way upon you.

A group of people had complained to the Prophetsaww of what tended to present to them because it was easier for them if the wind were to sweep them away or a beloved one would be cut off from them, than that they should be speaking about it. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘You are finding that (to be so)?’ They said, ‘Yes’. So hesaww said: ‘By the Oneazwj in Whose Hand is mysaww soul! That is explicit Emān. So whenever you find it to be so, so you should be saying,
‘We believe in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and in His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, and there is neither any Might or Strength except with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’’’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad (all them) from Ali ibn Mahziyar who has said the following: “

A man wrote to abu Ja’far (a.s.) and complained about what would pass in his mind. The Imam answered him in certain parts of his words: ‘If Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, wills, He will keep you steadfast and He will not allow Satan to find way in you.

Certain people complained to the Holy Prophet for what happened in their mind so much so that they liked to be blown away by the wind or being cut in pieces than to speak out of that thing in their mind. The Messenger of Allah asked, ‘Do you find that?’ They said, ‘Yes we do.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘By the One in whose hands is my soul that it is clear belief. Whenever you sense it say, “
We believe in Allah and His Messenger and there is no means and power without Allah.’”
